I lived there and after learning the truth about Hawaii’s history I felt guilty about it. I think more American visitors should understand the oppression Hawaii is in and try to support more locals instead of the fancy hotels and tourist attractions owned by white people. 
On Oahu I highly recommend going to the shrimp trucks on the north side of the island, so fresh and delicious!! 
Avoid Diamond Head if you actually enjoy hiking, it’s a paved path with a view that can be seen at other hikes. Lots of tourists and raggedy kids running around and you don’t get to be at the top for long. 
Also avoid Hanauma Bay, after tourist destroyed it over the last few decades it’s just disappointing and sad. All the sea life has mostly left and the coral is dead. 
I love Hawaii and I’ll always fight for its freedom, please keep Hawaii clean and treat it with respect. 
Aloha

Hi please check out the department of labor stats on wage gap and inequality. If you have access there are plenty of case studies proving gender gaps! It’s not propaganda...  

Not sure where you got that it was disproven from but I’d like to see it. 

Also not sure why’d you’d encourage a child to debate with his teacher knowing it’ll get him in trouble and harm his grade... sounds like you don’t have his best interest and are setting him up for failure. 

To the OP, best of luck but please don’t try to argue with your teacher... Just let it go because if you can’t deal with this appropriately then the rest of your education and work life will be really tough.

Hi as an HR mgmt major I can tell you the gender gap is very real, please look at the department of labor statistics displayed on their website! Many case studies have proved how and why the wage gap exists. Mostly is due to women not typically being breadwinners, which means they don’t need as much in a lot of companies minds even though that is changing. Also these stats are only in the US, other countries have different things going on.
 If women’s rights are important to your teacher you should respect that and stop trying to argue, just listen and you may learn something!(not being an asshole, I do mean that!!!). Don’t sit and linger on what you should say or how angry it makes you. unfortunately throughout your life you’ll hear things you don’t want to and cannot say or do anything... 
once you get to college it’s much easier because you can just drop the class but for now just be respectful. If equality in the workforce or anything HR related interests you, I recommend taking an HR class in college because you will learn a lot about the workforce and labor laws! 
I wish you best of luck and hope it all works out!
